logline: Eight episodes, eight characters, one collapsing world - each instalment a single continuous take following a different ordinary person during the first hours of civilisation's unravelling in France.

bollymeter.basis: Nominated for the International Emmy Award for Best TV Movie or Miniseries in 2020 (48th ceremony) - a signal of the series' exceptional formal ambition: eight episodes, each shot in a single continuous take.

seasons.review_body: L'Effondrement arrived on Canal+ in late 2019 as one of the most formally radical miniseries produced in France - eight episodes, each presenting a different character and location during the initial hours of a civilisational collapse, and each shot in a single continuous take with no cuts. Directed by the collective Les Parasites (Guillaume Desjardins, Bastien Ughetto, Jimmy Laporal-Trésor, and Jérémy Bernard), the series rejected the conventional disaster-narrative grammar of cross-cutting and parallel editing in favour of something rawer and more immersive. The anthology structure mirrors the chaos: individual lives fragmented, each episode a sealed bottle floating in the same catastrophe. The series received an International Emmy nomination for Best TV Movie or Miniseries at the 48th ceremony in 2020 - one of four international contenders in the category. Critics who covered it for English-language outlets noted the extraordinary formal constraint and its effect: without cuts to compress time or shift perspective, the collapse unfolds at human pace.

episode_reviews.title: The Supermarket
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The opening episode follows a supermarket manager as shelves are stripped and the social contract dissolves in real time - a single unbroken take that refuses to look away from the mundane logistics of panic.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The moment when the manager realises that her authority has simply ceased to function - no violence, just absence.

episode_reviews.title: The Finale
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The final episode draws the anthology's threads together by choosing a perspective that sees the collapse from the outside - a single take that confirms the scope of what the preceding seven hours have only partially revealed.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The closing image - which the series has been building toward without the audience realising it until it arrives.
